description_good_justification: The README opens with what Mimic is: a native macOS app, with a CLI, that runs local mock API servers. https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/README.md
interact_justification: The README covers installing (Homebrew cask or signed pkg), and feedback and contributions go through GitHub issues and pull requests. https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/issues
contribution_justification: Contributions are pull requests on GitHub; the process is in https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
contribution_requirements_justification: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md lists build and test commands, test gates and what CI requires; https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/AGENTS.md lists code rules.
documentation_interface_justification: The CLI and control API are documented in https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/docs/CLI.md
sites_https_justification: The repository, releases and website (https://mimic-mock.app) are served over HTTPS only.
discussion_justification: GitHub issues and pull requests are public, searchable and linkable: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/issues
english_justification: All documentation and discussion is in English.
repo_track_justification: Git records who changed what and when; every change lands through a pull request with CI.
repo_interim_justification: Work happens in public branches and pull requests between releases.
version_unique_justification: Each release has a unique version and git tag: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/releases
version_tags_justification: Every release is tagged (v0.14.0, v0.16.0, ...): https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/tags
release_notes_justification: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md in Keep a Changelog format, plus notes on each GitHub release.
release_notes_vulns_justification: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md has a Security section for any release that fixes a vulnerability.
report_process_justification: Bugs and feature requests go to GitHub issues: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/issues
report_responses_justification: The external request in the last year (#75, pass-through of real calls) was implemented and closed: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/issues?q=is%3Aissue
enhancement_responses_justification: Enhancement requests are answered or implemented, for example #75: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/issues/75
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: Private reports go through GitHub private security advisories, as https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/SECURITY.md says: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/security/advisories/new
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received in the last 6 months.
build_justification: SwiftPM (swift build) builds the portable modules and CLI; Tuist and xcodebuild build the macOS app.
build_floss_tools_justification: The portable modules and CLI build with the open-source Swift toolchain; the macOS app needs Xcode.
test_justification: swift test and xcodebuild test run unit and UI suites; documented in https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#test-gates
test_invocation_justification: swift test (portable modules) and xcodebuild test (app), as CONTRIBUTING.md documents.
test_most_justification: Unit suites cover every module and XCUITest covers the app's flows; line coverage is published as a README badge.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions runs the tests on every pull request and the full suite nightly: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/actions
test_policy_justification: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/AGENTS.md requires tests for every changed happy, error, empty and edge flow.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent changes add tests with the code, for example the fuzzing PR #161 added a regression test for the crash it fixed.
warnings_justification: Swift 6 language mode with strict concurrency checking; CI reports first-party Release-build warnings on every run.
warnings_fixed_justification: Compiler warnings in first-party code are fixed as CI reports them.
warnings_strict_justification: Warnings are reported in CI, not treated as errors.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles: least privilege (App Sandbox, Hardened Runtime), a loopback-only control API with a per-instance token, and input validation on imports. See https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/SECURITY.md
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer knows the common error classes for this kind of software (injection, path traversal, untrusted input parsing, token leakage) and the mitigations used; untrusted importers are fuzzed.
crypto_published_justification: Mimic implements no cryptographic algorithms; TLS and code signing come from the OS and Apple's tooling.
crypto_pfs_justification: Mimic implements no key agreement protocols.
crypto_random_justification: The only secret Mimic creates, the control API token, is 32 bytes from SystemRandomNumberGenerator, the platform CSPRNG: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/Sources/ControlPlane/ControlEndpointFile.swift
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases download over HTTPS from GitHub; the pkg is Developer ID signed and notarized by Apple; the Homebrew cask pins its SHA-256; releases carry build provenance and SBOM attestations.
delivery_unsigned_justification: Hashes are only ever fetched over HTTPS (the Homebrew cask), and the pkg itself is signed and notarized.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: Dependabot alerts are on and none are open; dependency review blocks pull requests that add a known-vulnerable dependency.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No known critical vulnerabilities are open.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: No credentials are in the repository; secret scanning and push protection are on, and release secrets live in an approval-gated GitHub environment.
static_analysis_justification: CodeQL analyses Swift, Python, Ruby and the GitHub Actions workflows: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/.github/workflows/codeql.yml
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security queries look for common vulnerabilities.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open CodeQL alerts.
static_analysis_often_justification: CodeQL runs on every pull request and push to main (Swift nightly).
dynamic_analysis_justification: libFuzzer with AddressSanitizer fuzzes the HAR and OpenAPI importers and the project and control-command decoders on every change to them and nightly: https://github.com/srpadrono/mimic/blob/main/Fuzz/README.md
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: First-party code is Swift, a memory-safe language; the fuzzers still run under AddressSanitizer.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: Fuzz builds keep Swift's runtime checks, which trap on overflow, out-of-range access and failed preconditions.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: Fuzzing findings are fixed with regression tests; the first, a crash on malformed OpenAPI files, was fixed in PR #161.
